verses.text: Jesus also told his disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his property.
He called the manager in and said, ‘What’s this I hear about you? Turn in your accounts, because you can’t be my manager anymore.’
“The manager thought to himself, ‘What will I do now? My master is taking away my job. I’m not strong enough to dig, and I’m too ashamed to beg.
I know what I’ll do, so people will welcome me into their homes after I lose my job.’
He called in each of his master’s debtors. He asked the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
The man answered, ‘A hundred measures of olive oil.’ The manager said, ‘Take your bill, sit down quickly, and change it to fifty.’
Then he asked another, ‘How much do you owe?’ He answered, ‘A hundred measures of wheat.’ The manager said, ‘Take your bill and change it to eighty.’
“The master praised the dishonest manager because he’d acted shrewdly. People of this world are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than people who belong to the light.
I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it’s gone, you’ll be welcomed into eternal homes.
Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
So if you haven’t been trustworthy with worldly wealth, who will trust you with true riches?
And if you haven’t been trustworthy with someone else’s property, who will give you property of your own?
“No servant can serve two masters. They’ll hate one and love the other, or be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and money.”
The Pharisees, who loved money, heard all this and sneered at Jesus.
He said to them, “You’re the ones who make yourselves look righteous in front of people, but God knows your hearts. What people value highly is disgusting to God.
“The law and the prophets were proclaimed until John. Since then, the good news of God’s kingdom has been preached, and everyone is pressing their way into it.
But it’s easier for heaven and earth to disappear than for even the smallest stroke of a letter in the law to fail.
“Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery. And anyone who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.
“There was a rich man who dressed in purple and fine linen and lived in luxury every day.
A poor man named Lazarus, covered with sores, was laid at the rich man’s gate.
He longed to eat the scraps falling from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
The poor man died, and angels carried him to Abraham’s side. The rich man also died and was buried.
In Hades, where he was suffering, the rich man looked up and saw Abraham far away, with Lazarus beside him.
He called out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me! Send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I’m in agony in this fire.’
“But Abraham said, ‘Child, remember that during your life you received good things, while Lazarus received bad things. Now he’s comforted here, and you’re suffering.
Besides, a wide chasm has been fixed between us and you. Those who want to cross from here to you can’t, and no one can cross from there to us.’
“The rich man said, ‘Then please, father, send Lazarus to my father’s house—
I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so they won’t end up in this place of torment too.’
“But Abraham said, ‘They have Moses and the prophets. They should listen to them.’
“‘No, father Abraham,’ the man said. ‘But if someone goes to them from the dead, they’ll turn back to God.’
“Abraham said, ‘If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, they won’t be convinced even if someone rises from the dead.’”
